rows.question: Can Mogg Fanatic assign combat damage, sacrifice itself in response, and still deal that combat damage?

Quote [Ruling, 2011-01-01]: "You control the player while this spell is resolving, which means you get to see anything they can see. If that player is required to search their library as part of playing the card or as part of its resolution if it's cast as a spell, then you can see the cards in that player's library as well."

The complete current Oracle text must be quoted, including the mana-ability restrictions, which appear nowhere on the Alpha printing."

rows.question: How does Time Vault's current Oracle text differ from what is printed on the Alpha card, and which governs?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Current Oracle text governs over the Alpha printed text, and the two differ in how Time Vault untaps and how the extra turn is taken.
Missing: None
Why: The Alpha card let you untap Time Vault at will by skipping a turn as an activated-style cost, and the tap ability simply granted an extra turn. The current Oracle text instead makes the untap an optional replacement effect that you choose as your turn would begin (only if the artifact is tapped), and the extra-turn ability now costs the tap symbol and the artifact enters tapped. Oracle governs over printed wording under CR 108.1, so the modern text is what is played. The only decision document on point is model-assisted and not human-confirmed, so I treat it as a reviewed draft rather than a settled holding.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording").
Quote [Oracle — Time Vault, current]: This artifact enters tapped.
This artifact doesn't untap during your untap step.
If you would begin your turn while this artifact is tapped, you may skip that turn instead. If you do, untap this artifact.
{T}: Take an extra turn after this one.
Quote [Printed — Limited Edition Alpha (LEA, no. 274, released 1993-08-05)]: Tap to gain an additional turn after the current one. Time Vault doesn't untap normally during untap phase; to untap it, you must skip a turn. Time Vault begins tapped.
Quote [CR 108.1]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Quote [decision.Time-Vault.0.268, model-assisted draft]: Oracle governs under CR 108.1. Untapping changed from paying a skipped turn at will to an optional replacement when your turn would begin, which is why the notorious untap loops behave differently.
Quote [Time Vault ruling, 2008-10-01]: The choice of whether or not to skip a turn is made as that turn would begin, and only if Time Vault is tapped at that time. If you choose to skip your turn, Time Vault untaps before anything else happens in the next turn.
Quote [Time Vault ruling, 2008-10-01]: This wording means that you no longer end up skipping multiple turns if you find a way to activate the ability multiple times.
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: The Alpha printed text and the current Oracle text disagree on the untap mechanic: printed allows untapping by skipping a turn as an at-will choice, while Oracle makes it an optional replacement effect chosen as your turn would begin, and printed's "begins tapped" is reworded as "enters tapped." Oracle wins under CR 108.1.

rows.question: Is Chaos Orb's physical flip requirement still part of its Oracle text?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Yes. Chaos Orb's current Oracle text still requires the physical flip — flipping it onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot and turning over completely at least once.
Missing: None
Why: The Oracle wording retrieved for Chaos Orb retains the flip instruction verbatim as part of the activated ability, so the physical requirement was not removed in errata. A verified case document posing this exact question answers affirmatively and notes the wording was retemplated but the physical requirement remains. The 2019 ruling that supplies a different (Old School) text is format-specific and does not displace the Oracle wording for normal play.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), as applied by the verified case case.rv-Chaos-Orb.
Quote [Oracle text (card.edb455f4-8dc9-4b7c-b25c-cb51b7dfbb41)]: {1}, {T}: If this artifact is on the battlefield, flip it onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot. If this artifact turns over completely at least once during the flip, destroy all nontoken permanents it touches. Then destroy this artifact.
Quote [Printed text, Limited Edition Alpha (printing.92274971-7c4a-4326-b0fe-75e2d124f718)]: {1}: Flip Chaos Orb onto the playing area from a height of at least one foot. Chaos Orb must turn completely over at least once or it is discarded with no effect. When Chaos Orb lands, any cards in play that it touches are destroyed, as is Chaos Orb.
Quote [Ruling, 2004-10-04]: It must flip 360 degrees (that's what "flip" means). And this flip must be in the air and not in your hand.
Quote [Verified case verdict (case.rv-Chaos-Orb)]: Yes. Current Oracle text still requires flipping the card onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot, and it must turn over completely at least once. The wording was retemplated but the physical requirement remains.

If Chaos Orb is on the battlefield, flip Chaos Orb onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot. If Chaos Orb turns over completely at least once during the flip, and lands resting on the chosen permanent, destroy that permanent. Then destroy Chaos Orb."
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: The 2019-01-27 ruling supplies a distinct Oracle-style text for the Old School format (single chosen permanent, "lands resting on"), which differs from the general Oracle text retrieved on the card; that ruling is scoped to Old School play only. The unconfirmed model-assisted decision decision.Chaos-Orb.0.346 discusses only the added {T} cost and token exclusion and is silent on the flip, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the flip's presence; the verified case is the controlling authority here.

rows.question: The printed card just says 'Bands'. What does the card actually do, and did its function change?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: The card is Benalish Hero, whose printed "Bands" is the banding keyword; current Oracle spells out banding with reminder text, and the corpus's reviewed text-difference records classify every wording version — including the Alpha printing — as nonfunctional, so its function did not change.
Missing: The Comprehensive Rules paragraph that defines the banding ability (cross-referenced as 702.22) is not present in the retrieved corpus — only 100.2, 100.4, 101.1, 108.1, 510.1, 510.2, 608.2 and 700.2 were retrieved — so the rules-level definition of banding cannot be quoted here, only the Oracle reminder text, the glossary entry and the Wizards rulings. Also, none of the 20 retrieved reviewed decision documents covers Benalish Hero, so no card-specific reviewed decision exists for this question.
Why: The only card in the corpus matching "Bands" is Benalish Hero, a {W} Creature — Human Soldier, and its Alpha printing's entire rules text is the single word "Bands." Oracle now renders that same keyword as "Banding" followed by reminder text describing bands, group blocking and the banding controller's damage assignment. Each printing's stored difference record is marked "nonfunctional," which is the corpus's own reviewed judgment that the rewording did not alter how the card works.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), which supersedes the printed wording of any individual printing.
Quote [Alpha (LEA) printed text, printing.11600105]: Bands
Quote [Fifth Edition (5ED) printed text, printing.32dcd608]: Banding
Quote [Current Oracle text, Benalish Hero]: Banding (Any creatures with banding, and up to one without, can attack in a band. Bands are blocked as a group. If any creatures with banding you control are blocking or being blocked by a creature, you divide that creature's combat damage, not its controller, among any of the creatures it's being blocked by or is blocking.)
Quote [Glossary, "Banding, "Bands with Other""]: Banding is a keyword ability that modifies the rules for declaring attackers and assigning combat damage. "Bands with other" is a specialized version of the ability. See rule 702.22, "Banding."
Quote [Ruling 2008-10-01-0]: If a creature with banding attacks, it can team up with any number of other attacking creatures with banding (and up to one nonbanding creature) and attack as a unit called a "band." The band can be blocked by any creature that could block a single creature in the band. Blocking any creature in a band blocks the entire band. If a creature with banding is blocked, the attacking player chooses how the blockers' damage is assigned.
Quote [Ruling 2008-10-01-1]: A maximum of one nonbanding creature can join an attacking band no matter how many creatures with banding are in it.
Quote [Ruling 2008-10-01-2]: Creatures in the same band must all attack the same player or planeswalker.
Quote [Ruling 2009-10-01-3]: If a creature in combat has banding, its controller assigns damage for creatures blocking or blocked by it.
Quote [CR 108.1]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: The Alpha, Beta and Unlimited printings say "Bands"; the Fourth and Fifth Edition printings say "Banding"; Oracle carries the keyword plus full reminder text. Oracle wins under CR 108.1, and the corpus's textDifference records mark all five printings (including the "Bands" Alpha printing, similarity 0.025) as "nonfunctional," i.e. the rewording changed no function.

rows.question: My Alpha Lightning Bolt says 'one target'. Can I still point it at a planeswalker?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Yes — under current Oracle wording Lightning Bolt reads "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target," and "any target" includes planeswalkers (and battles), so an Alpha copy may be pointed at a planeswalker.
Missing: None
Why: CR 108.1 directs you to the Oracle card reference to determine a card's wording, so the old Alpha text does not control how the card plays today. The verified case record for exactly this question resolves it in the affirmative, citing "any target" as the operative wording, and the reviewed decision record for the Alpha/Beta printings states that "one target" became "any target," adding planeswalkers and battles. The difference is flagged as functional despite a high measured text similarity of 0.600 between the Alpha text and Oracle text.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1, which makes the Oracle reference the source of a card's wording; this is recorded in the reviewed decision decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6 and the verified adjudication case case.rv-Lightning-Bolt.
